propositions: Batching multiple candidates into one LLM call reduces the total number of judge() calls from 2N to 2*ceil(N/batch_size), eliminating redundant system prompt transmissions and saving ~8,460 tokens on a 6-candidate corpus

The cacheable prefix (base prompt + hoisted query digest + batch protocol section) grows from 873 tokens to 1,337 tokens, crossing the 1024-token minimum threshold and enabling prefix caching with write 1,331 and read 1,331 tokens
Verdict demultiplexing by candidate label (not position) ensures each candidate receives exactly one verdict; missing or malformed entries abstain only that candidate without affecting others

Real-API measurement on claude-sonnet-4-6 over identical corpus shows 12 calls/18,494 input tokens (8415 baseline) reducing to 2 calls/9,116 input tokens (−50.7%), with cache writing and reading 1,331 tokens per call
Relation label shift is systematic and conservative: 6 of 12 ordered pairs shift labels, mostly toward unrelated; within-build noise is 1–3 pairs, confirming the shift is not sampling variance

A positive control (query's own digest as seventh candidate) recovers duplicates verdict at full confidence in both orderings with identical cited artifact, confirming true positives survive batching without cross-contamination
